from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        input_prompt = Text("Input Prompt", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        input_group = VGroup(input_prompt, camera_icon).arrange(DOWN)
        
        neural_pipeline = Rectangle(height=1.5, width=2.5, color="#ADD8E6", fill_opacity=0.3)
        pipeline_label = Text("Neural Pipeline", font_size=20, color="#ADD8E6").move_to(neural_pipeline.get_center())
        pipeline_group = VGroup(neural_pipeline, pipeline_label, computer_icon).arrange(DOWN)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Diffusion adds noise to an image, destroying its structure.",
            "A neural network learns to predict this added noise.",
            "Reversing this process recovers the image from noise."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Diffusion Process: Math as an Artist", lecture_lines)
        
        # Load Assets
        canvas = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/canvas.svg")
        noise = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/noise.svg")
        
        # Applying requested fixes
        self.place_at_grid(canvas, 'D4', scale_factor=1.1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(noise, 'B5', scale_factor=0.6)
        noise.set_color("#808080")
        self.play(FadeIn(canvas), FadeIn(noise))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        net_text = Text("Neural Network", font_size=20, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(net_text, 'B4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(net_text))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Sequential transformation
        step_frames = 5
        target = Circle(radius=0.3, color=GREEN).set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(target, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Animate noise to target (simulated reversal)
        self.play(
            Transform(noise, target, run_time=3),
            FadeOut(net_text)
        )
        
        # Glowing effect
        glow = Circle(radius=0.4, color=YELLOW).set_stroke(width=4)
        self.place_at_grid(glow, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(glow))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

            "The process uses 50 to 100 small steps.",
            "The final result is art born from noise."
        ])
        
        # Load Assets

        self.play(image_icon.animate.scale(1.2).set_color("#FFFFFF"), run_time=1.0)

outline.topic: The Magic of Text-to-Image AI: Diffusion, CLIP, and the Math Behind the Art
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic background in linear algebra and probability.

sections.title: Introduction: The Image Synthesis Pipeline
sections.content: A 30-second overview of how text prompts transform into high-resolution images. Introduce the two pillars: CLIP (the 'Understanding' bridge) and Diffusion (the 'Creation' engine).
sections.example: Visualizing a text prompt 'A robot painting a sunset' turning into a pixelated sketch, then a refined image.

sections.title: CLIP: Mapping Language to Visual Space
sections.content: Explain Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP). Concept: Mapping text and image embeddings into a shared high-dimensional vector space using cosine similarity. Prerequisite: Dot products measure alignment.
sections.example: A graph showing an image vector and a text vector pointing in the same direction in 3D space, showing their 'alignment' score.

sections.title: The Diffusion Process: Math as an Artist
sections.content: Introduce Forward Diffusion (adding Gaussian noise) and Reverse Diffusion (denoising). Math concept: Markov Chains. We learn a neural network to predict the noise component ε at each step t.
sections.example: An animation of a clear photo of a 'Golden Retriever' gradually turning into static white noise, then reversing the process.

sections.title: Guidance: Bridging Text and Noise
sections.content: Explain how the CLIP embedding influences the denoising step. We use 'Classifier-Free Guidance' to push the diffusion model to predict noise that aligns better with the text prompt vector.
sections.example: A vector field showing the noise-prediction gradient being 'tilted' or steered by the text input toward the desired image content.

sections.title: Synthesis and Conclusion
sections.content: Summarize the iterative refinement process. The model starts with pure noise and performs 50-100 denoising steps, each steered by CLIP, to arrive at a coherent image.
sections.example: A summary graphic: [Prompt] -> [CLIP Embedding] -> [Denoising Loop] -> [High-Res Image of a Cyberpunk City].
